en: The Scripture on the Dharma of Pride Spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmakṣema of the Western Jin Dynasty.
The Buddha told Ānanda: "There are those who, after serving the Buddha, immediately become wealthy and noble; there are those who..."
"The Buddha has subsequently met with decline and misfortune.
Ānanda asked the Buddha,
"How is it that while both served the Buddha, their fortunes— one declining and the other prospering— were so different?"
"Why is this so? The Buddha said to Ānanda,
"When one serves the Buddha, one should seek out an enlightened teacher."
Those who have attained clear realization proceed from the method of receiving the precepts;
in order to eliminate all conceptualizations, they accord with the sūtras;
they practice with diligence and do not lose the teaching.

One who receives [these] does not transgress; as for "even those as small as a hair," such a person does not violate the prohibitions of the Path. They are constantly guarded and protected by the various devas and benevolent spirits; whatever they undertake meets with success, their wealth and profit increase a hundredfold, and they are revered by all people. In the future, they shall attain Buddhahood—how much more so regarding worldly riches and benefits!
Such people as these serve the Buddha and are true disciples of the Buddha.
Furthermore, there are others who serve the Buddha but do not encounter an enlightened teacher, nor do they possess scriptures or images, and they do not even pay homage or show reverence.
Without knowledge or understanding, they insistently teach others to receive the Dharma-precepts, yet they lack ultimate faith.
After receiving the precepts, they willfully violate them once again.
Their minds are clouded and obscure, filled with hesitation; they are unwilling to read the sutras, practice the Way, or cultivate merit, believing at one moment and disbelieving at another.
Furthermore, they are unable to maintain mindfulness on the days of the fast, nor do they offer incense, light lamps, or perform prostrations.

Consequently, they give rise to anger and resentment, shouting and reviling; they curse as they come and go, their mouths never remaining closed, harboring hatred and jealousy in their hearts, and even inciting others to take life.
When seeing scriptures or images with their own eyes, they lack any heart of reverence.

If they possess scriptures, they merely hang them upon a wall, or cast them upon a bed or mat, or place them within old clothes, tattered bedding, or worn-out baskets; or they handle them with the impure hands of their wives, children, or young sons;
they let them be blackened by smoke and ruined by leaks from the roof, no longer even looking upon them.
Furthermore, if one does not burn incense, light lamps, or pay homage toward it, it will be no different from secular scriptures.
Virtuous deities will abandon it, while evil spirits will find opportunity to seize it; they will pursue it without ceasing, leading to its decline and illness.
Suddenly falling ill, he became terrified and hesitant, thinking to himself:
"I have only recently begun serving the Buddha; why then have I fallen ill?
Unable to trust himself, he summoned a physician.

Divinations by physicians, rites of exorcism, and suppressive charms were of no avail; they consequently prayed to and made offerings to heterodox deities, whereby their transgressions increased further.
Malevolent spirits and evil ghosts took up station at their gates, leading to ruin and death that never left their doorways.
Their wealth will diminish, and their family members will suffer from illnesses that pass from one to another, never leaving their beds.
At the end of their lives, they will fall into the Hell of Mud and Plows, where they shall undergo interrogation, punishment, and penalization for countless years.

This person merely sits, yet cannot concentrate; their will is hesitant and they have no firm foundation. Because they do not believe in the Buddha-dharma, they incur such calamities and suffer such decline and exhaustion.

"Those people in the world who do not understand the Buddha-dharma claim that serving the Buddha brings about misfortune and decline; they fail to realize that it is their own conduct that is improper and that they have violated the precepts of the Buddhist scriptures."
"With a mind solely intent on doing evil, one possesses every manner of depravity; the body itself invites this retribution—there is no one else who bestows it.
Upon hearing this, Ānanda bowed his head to the ground in prostration before the Buddha, paid homage, and joyfully put the teaching into practice.
The Sūtra on the Dharma of Pride Spoken by the Buddha
